key_insight: A cell-centric, interpretable pathology model (C3PRO) can match leading multiple-instance learning methods for pancreatic cancer diagnosis and outcome prediction while revealing named morphological phenotypes that pathologists can inspect.
clinical_relevance: This could improve trust and auditability of AI in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma workflows, supporting diagnosis, prognosis, and resectability assessment with understandable tissue-level features.
method: Extracted cell-centered embeddings from pathology foundation model tiles containing a cell and its neighborhood.
Clustered embeddings into recurrent morphological phenotypes and built a spatial graph to capture recurring tissue motifs.
Benchmarked C3PRO against four multiple-instance learning models and had expert pathologists review the phenotype vocabulary.
evidence_signal: In 809 patients across 825 diagnostic biopsies, C3PRO achieved on-par performance with strong baselines for diagnosis (AUC 0.958), survival (0.617), and resectability (0.696).
watch_item: The phenotype vocabulary and its prognostic value need external validation and careful integration into routine pathology workflows before clinical use.
paper_title: An interpretable cell-centric representation of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma matches multiple-instance learning for clinical outcomes and leads to novel pathologist-driven histological biomarkers
